rv.q: Moments of violence become freeze-frames amid jagged seizures, with actors shuddering, striking themselves and marching around the stage’s perimeter ritualistically touching or spitting on its corners. Standing out in a totally committed cast, Zackary Momoh’s Eben is a powerful presence.

But while you can’t help admire his heated, guttural vision, it stretches out the play’s action and ultimately threatens to overwhelm the drama it seeks to illuminate. One of O’Neill’s lesser-known plays – its last London production was in 2012 – Desire Under the Elms centres on a conflict over land and rightful inheritance.
Indeed the 2 hour and 40 minutes running time (including interval) vastly outstays its welcome.
It has an interesting story at its heart with the potential to shock and move, but it's bogged down with excess dialogue and can't punch through.
I could appreciate the intensity of what was unfolding without always feeling emotionally connected to it.

cn.t: Mixed reviews for this O'Neill revival — atmospheric lighting and sound earn praise, but the production feels like a tough, slow watch that never fully convinces.
